title: Prove the closed-disk boundary for reversible inward phase updates
head: 399aa4293d40061fad8ee7e55b39cd1491c7d917
body:
PR2527 supplies a norm-nonincreasing unit-phase product with error below `4h`. This contribution proves that the interface cannot also be a total exactly reversible destructive same-grid update on a complete fixed-helper disk fiber: for the valid rational phase `(3+4i)/5` and every `p>=3`, no injective self-map of the closed dyadic unit disk can satisfy both norm nonincrease and the error bound. At `p=1,2` the identity meets these three conditions, so the stated threshold is sharp.

The proof uses the standard finite-permutation norm argument and the four-point dyadic unit-circle shell. The new contribution is their precise source-contract application, not a new finite-set lemma. A complete restored helper state fixed independently of the varying input implies data injectivity. No linearity or bound on the number of restored dirty helpers is needed.

The actual unmodified PR2527 kernel is pinned and executed: zero and one real grid step collide at every precision (written proof plus checks through 128), and at p=3 the phase/conjugate roundtrip is `1 -> 1/2+3i/4 -> 3/4`. Both calls satisfy the original source contract. PR2527 does not promise reversibility; this is not a source defect. PR2549 motivates explicit precision/return premises but is not claimed to require inversion of this kernel.

Constructive controls show the boundary: retaining the exact product on the finer 2p grid preserves contraction and injection with an exact image inverse; standard rounded shear lifting is exactly reversible on the same full grid with squared error at most (153/80)h^2 but can leave the disk. Retaining the original input also permits exact dirty-accumulator compute/uncompute despite the phase kernel's collisions. Thus this is not a general strict-zero cleanup impossibility. Grid refinement, outward slack, restricted entrance domains, extra output or retained history change the premises.

Evidence: 17,118 complete-disk inputs at p=1..6; 68,472 Gaussian-unit cases; 128 collision precisions; 8 semantic controls; separate 13-shell/120-permutation/3,969 rational-shear checks; Git-free optimized read-only replay and 8 source/typed-receipt/CLI corruption controls. Five predecessor files are byte-for-byte retained with SHA-256/Git-blob pins, authenticated before executable imports. A separate Codex agent reviewed the proof and code and independently replayed the scientific checks with CPython 3.12.7, finding no blocker. No independent human, proof-assistant, hosted CI or full selected cold replay is claimed.
